## Question 2 (10-points)

Create a level-1 section header at the top of your document at label it *Packages*. Next, under a Question-2 level two section header, make a code chunk and library the aRtsy package. We are going to use a function in this package to plot the Collatz conjecture. On your own, research and explain what the Collatz conjecture is. Then, write the Collatz conjecture equation using in-line LaTex code. 

$f(n) = \frac{n}{2} \quad \text{if } n \text{ is even}$

$f(n) = 3n + 1 \quad \text{if } n \text{ is odd}$

*The latex code looks like this:* 

```
$f(n) = \frac{n}{2} \quad \text{if } n \text{ is even}$

$f(n) = 3n + 1 \quad \text{if } n \text{ is odd}$
```

*This conjecture states that no matter what starting positive integer you choose, the sequence will always eventually reach 1 (and then loop infinitely in the cycle $4 \to 2 \to 1$).*

## Question 3 (10-points)

Please see the following function `canvas_collatz()` from the `aRtsy` package in R. In 2-3 sentences, describe what this function is doing. 


```{r}
#| eval: false
#| echo: true

set.seed(3)

canvas_collatz(
  colors = c("blue"),
  n = 10
)
```

*This code is picking 10 random numbers, and plotting their path with a blue line as it approaches 1, following the rules of the conjecture*. 

### part b 

When you run the above code multiple times, you get different output. With this information... 

-- Explain why you get different out every time you run the code

-- Explain why this might be troublesome when trying to put this code into your .qmd file

-- Pull the help file up for `set.seed()`, and explain how this can be used to make sure we get the same result every time. Then, use the `set.seed()` function correctly with your favorite number, and include the code above in a code chunk.

*The `canvas_collatz()` function uses a random process. The argument `n = 10` is giving us 10 random numbers. Each time we run the code, a new random process takes place, giving us 10 new random numbers and thus a new picture*. 

*This might be troublesome because the picture will change every time we Render are document. This means that it will be impossible to describe the picture in our .qmd!*

*The `set.seed()` function ensures that the random state is fixed every time some code is run. This helps statisticians with reproducibility in simulation studies. The process of picking the numbers in the `canvas_collatz()` is still random, but those 10 random numbers are now fixed with `set.seed()`.*

## Question 4 (10-points)

Contrast the code below with the code shown in question 3. What is this code doing differently than the previous chunk? That is, what's different both in the code, and the corresponding result? Next, explain if it would be appropriate to include `set.seed(1)` with the code below.

```{r}
#| eval: false 
#| echo: true

canvas_collatz(
  colors = c("blue"),
  n = 1:20
)
```

*Now that you are passing a vector of values as the input to the argument n, the help file says that these become the starting integers that will pass through the conjecture. This is no longer a random process, and `set.seed(1)` is unnecessary, because there is not a random process assocciated with the code above*.
